# mongodb_db_collection (Resource)

Provides a MongoDB collection.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "mongodb_db_collection" "collection_1" {
  db                                = "my_database"
  name                              = "example"
  change_stream_pre_and_post_images = true
  deletion_protection               = true
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `db` (String) Database in which the collection is created. Changing it forces a new collection.
- `name` (String) Collection name. Changing it forces a new collection.

### Optional

- `change_stream_pre_and_post_images` (Boolean) Whether to record the full document before and after each change for [change streams](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/changeStreams/#change-streams-with-document-pre--and-post-images) (`changeStreamPreAndPostImages`). Defaults to `false`.
- `deletion_protection` (Boolean) Prevents Terraform from dropping the collection: destroying the resource fails while this is `true`. This is a provider-side setting, not stored in MongoDB. Defaults to `true`.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Base64-encoded ID of the collection, in the format `db.collection`.

## Import

In Terraform v1.5.0 and later, use an [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) to import the resource using its ID:

```terraform
import {
  to = mongodb_db_collection.example_collection
  id = "dGVzdF9kYi5jb2xsZWN0aW9uX3Rlc3Q=" # base64 of "test_db.collection_test"
}
```

The `terraform import` command can also be used:

```shell
# The ID is the base64-encoded "db.collection",
# e.g. for collection "collection_test" in database "test_db":
printf '%s' "test_db.collection_test" | base64
# dGVzdF9kYi5jb2xsZWN0aW9uX3Rlc3Q=

terraform import mongodb_db_collection.example_collection dGVzdF9kYi5jb2xsZWN0aW9uX3Rlc3Q=
```
